getting_started.intro: Follow this order when first setting up WinProx for your organisation.

admin_portal.title: Statuses — administrative portal
admin_portal.intro: These statuses are used by administrators to monitor and control the full workflow.
admin_portal.new: The issue has been created; at least one task is waiting for the team to start.
admin_portal.in_progress: Work on the issue is in progress; at least one task is being executed.
admin_portal.done: All tasks for this issue have been completed by the team; the administrator can now approve and close.
admin_portal.closed: The administrator has confirmed completion; the issue is finally closed.

internet_portal.title: Statuses — internet portal
internet_portal.intro: These statuses are aimed at workers in the field and citizens (reporters) to show the direct status of a specific task.
internet_portal.new: The task has been created and is waiting for the team to start.
internet_portal.in_progress: The team is currently on site carrying out the work.
internet_portal.done: The work has been completed by the worker and reported as finished.
internet_portal.closed: The task has been reviewed by the administrator and finally closed.

step_1_text: Assemble operational teams, add workers and assign a team leader. Link teams to specific categories so tasks always reach the right professionals. Workers sign in easily with their name and a personal icon. You can also add teams and workers in one go via a bulk import (CSV file).
step_2_text: Group units into categories (for example: drills, sanitary, fitness equipment, office or electricity). These categories help filter and organise your assets and are fully tailored to your sector. By linking teams to specific categories, WinProx ensures tasks are always picked up by the right team. Additionally, add locations (such as sites, buildings or floors) and create your units per location: these are the physical machines, spaces or objects for which issues and tasks are registered. Locations and units can also be uploaded via a bulk import (CSV file).
step_3_text: Print the unit QR from the location or unit detail page and the Clock Point QR from the team page. Attach both in a clearly visible place (for example on machines, printers, office furniture or at the entrance). Users scan the unit QR to directly open the portal, where they can submit issues and consult documents or announcements. Workers first scan the Clock Point QR to sign in (name + icon). They then scan the unit QR on site to record GPS, take photos and start or complete tasks. With the optional Time module they can also clock in and out via the Clock Point QR.
step_4_text: Issues come in via a QR scan or manual entry. For each issue, a task is automatically created and directly linked to the responsible team. It is possible to create multiple tasks for one issue (for example for both the technical team and the cleaning crew). Simply set a deadline and track progress closely via the dashboard and the calendar.
step_5_text: Workers carry out tasks on site via the unit QR portal (after signing in via Clock Point QR). Once all tasks for an issue have been handled, the administrator can definitively close the issue. All actions remain clearly visible in the audit trail. With the optional ESG module you can also record measurement values during recurring inspections — see the chapters ESG measurements and Measurements. With the optional Time module you record presence, breaks and work shifts — see the chapters Presence and Clock Points.
